claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: Adding ℓ−k isolated K2 components is an equivalence-preserving reduction: connected H3 must lie wholly within one component, and every added terminal pair has only its isolated edge as a connecting path. Restricting or extending a linkage therefore gives both directions. For k=1, connectivity is sufficient because a shortest terminal-to-terminal path has no chord, and BFS/DFS gives linear time. For fixed k, at most n listed path vertices form a polynomial certificate whose endpoints, edges, vertex-disjointness, individual inducedness, and absence of inter-path edges are directly checkable.
claims.witness: For each added pair, use the two endpoints of a fresh isolated K2 and its unique one-edge path.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction and certificate proof, supplemented by exact exhaustive enumeration of 10,650 labeled instances on at most five original vertices; connectivity versus induced-path existence and one-pair-to-two-pair padding equivalence both held in every case.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: If u-x-y-v is a geodesic of length three and deg(u),deg(v)≥3, choose two neighbors of u other than x and two of v other than y. Geodesicity excludes all central-path collisions and excludes a common neighbor of u and v, so these eight distinct vertices and seven selected edges form H3; extra edges are irrelevant for subgraph containment. If a graph were not 6-degenerate, some subgraph would have minimum degree at least seven. Root H3 and embed its remaining seven vertices parent-first: at step j≤8, the parent has at most j−2≤6 already used possible neighbors, hence an unused neighbor. Thus H3 embeds, a contradiction. K7 proves sharpness. Summing at most min(6,n−i) later neighbors in a degeneracy order gives 6n−21 for n≥7. Finally, the first four vertices of any geodesic of length at least three contradict the distance-three property when minimum degree is at least three.
claims.witness: K7 is H3-free because H3 has eight vertices, has degeneracy six, and has 21=6·7−21 edges.
claims.search_method: Universal embedding and geodesic arguments, plus exact exhaustive checks of all labeled graphs through six vertices, 141,532 high-degree vertex-pair distance cases, the K7 sharp witness, and an explicit H3 embedding in K8.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so both degree-three centers of any H3 would have to be original vertices. A three-edge path starting at an original vertex either enters an R-corridor and ends at its third subdivision vertex, or first uses its unique possible M-edge and then takes two forced corridor steps, again ending at a subdivision vertex. Thus no three-edge path joins two possible centers. Any path with original endpoints must traverse each entered four-edge corridor completely and therefore projects uniquely to a simple path in R∪M; lifting reverses this operation. Corridor interiors have no outside adjacencies. Consequently, the only possible chords or edges between lifted paths are M-edges, and inducedness is equivalent exactly to requiring every selected M-edge to be a consecutive used edge on one path. For M empty and R=K_m, contracting every corridor yields a K_m minor, so treewidth is at least m−1 and is unbounded.
claims.witness: The family G(K_m,∅) is H3-free and contains K_m as a minor for every m.
claims.search_method: Direct structural proof, supplemented by exact enumeration of 10,312 pairs (R,M) through five original vertices, 318,531 lifted one-path checks, 312 vertex-disjoint two-path checks through four original vertices, and clique constructions through seven original vertices. No H3 or correspondence failure was found.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: After deleting the b vertices B of degree at least three, every component is a path, isolated vertex, or cycle with at most two attachment edges. A terminal-free component can be used only as a complete corridor between two distinct vertices of B; one new degree-two representative per unordered B-pair suffices. In a terminal-bearing component, retain its terminals and B attachment occurrences as marks. Unmarked tails are unusable, while every gap between consecutive marks is either unused or traversed completely. Preserve a one-edge gap and replace a longer gap by a two-edge path, while retaining any original mark-to-mark adjacency so all chords and inter-path edges are preserved. A detached cycle with one terminal is an immediate NO instance. If such a component has t terminals, a path has at most t+1≤2t gaps and a cycle at most t gaps. Hence there are at most b retained branch vertices, 2k retained terminals, binom(b,2) generic corridor vertices, and 4k gap vertices, totaling b+binom(b,2)+6k. Suppression and expansion give inverse transformations on induced linkages. Exhaustive enumeration on the bounded compressed graph is a function only of k+b, establishing FPT.
claims.search_method: Component-by-component equivalence and vertex-count proof, supplemented by an exact implementation of the compression and exhaustive comparison on 26,202 labeled instances through five vertices with one or two terminal pairs; every original and compressed answer agreed and every stated size bound held.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: The stated graph has only seven vertices whereas H3 has eight, so it is H3-free. The paths s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2 are induced, vertex-disjoint, and anticomplete to each other. The unique shortest s1-t1 path is s1-x-t1, of length two. Because x is adjacent to the compulsory terminal s2, that shortest path is incompatible with every possible s2-t2 path. Thus fixing it changes a YES instance into failure.
claims.witness: Vertices {s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z}; edges {s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1}; valid linkage (s1-y-z-t1, s2-t2); unique greedy path s1-x-t1.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all induced paths for both terminal pairs, followed by direct chord, disjointness, and cross-edge tests. The checker found one unique shortest first-pair path and confirmed it is incompatible with the only induced second-pair path.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a complexity classification for every fixed k on H3-subgraph-free graphs. The draft proves polynomial-time solvability only for k=1. Its padding relation, structural restrictions, normal form, bounded-branching compression, and greedy counterexample are correct and materially illuminate the boundary, but none establishes either a polynomial-time algorithm or NP-completeness for any fixed k≥2. Therefore it does not fully resolve the target. The final writeup expressly says that the classification remains incomplete for k≥2, so it does not overclaim, and claimed_resolution="PARTIAL" is accurate.
checks_performed: Read the exact target and H3 definition from the authorized source input and the five proofs and final writeup from the authorized draft only.

Proved the distance-three obstruction, 6-degeneracy, sharpness, edge bound, and diameter consequence.
Proved H3-freeness and exact linkage correspondence for G(R,M), and verified the clique-minor treewidth family.
Reconstructed the bounded-branching compression, proved linkage preservation and the b+binom(b,2)+6k count.
